source.description:
PROBLEM
dist/ is committed and CI diffs it against a fresh build, so any bundle built against a
different dependency tree than CI's fails packed-smoke and payload-contract. That happened
four times on 2026-09-12 across #341, #342, #347 and a merge rebuild — every one of them a
src change whose author either did not rebuild, or rebuilt in a worktree whose node_modules
came from a plain `bun install`.

The subtle case is the one that cost the most time. In #347 the committed dist was rebuilt
and still failed. The CI diff showed only bundler-internal renaming — `process2` became
`process4` — which is not a behaviour difference at all; it means a different set of
modules was inlined because the dependency tree differed. CI installs with
`bun install --frozen-lockfile`; the worktree had a plain `bun install`. Rebuilding after
a frozen install produced a matching bundle.

An existing guard (unitAI-rrdnt.41) already refuses to build when a worktree has NO
node_modules, precisely because bun would resolve from the parent checkout and bake wrong
paths. It does not catch the adjacent case: node_modules present, but resolved without the
lockfile.

SUCCESS
A contributor cannot easily produce a dist that CI rejects. Either the build refuses or
warns when the install was not lockfile-frozen, or the failure names the real cause instead
of presenting a 90000-line bundle diff.

SCOPE
The build script and its existing guard, and whatever CI step emits the dist diff.

NON_GOALS
Do not stop committing dist/. That is a deliberate choice here and changing it is a much
larger decision.
Do not make CI regenerate and auto-commit dist — that would hide drift rather than catch it.

CONSTRAINTS
Any check must be cheap and deterministic; a build-time check that is itself
environment-sensitive would add a second flake source.
The existing guard's message is good and specific — extend that pattern rather than
introducing a different mechanism.

VALIDATION
- With a plain `bun install`, the build warns or refuses and names the lockfile as the cause.
- With `bun install --frozen-lockfile`, the build is silent and its output matches CI.
- Failing the dist diff in CI prints a line naming the likely cause, not only the diff.

OUTPUT
Four identical CI failures in one day becomes a message that says what to do.
source.title: dist/ CI failures are systemic: a non-frozen bun install in a worktree yields a bundle CI rejects
